 Qatar ready to welcome Asia’s rising cricket stars
 Published:
 18 Nov 2026 - 09:45 am
 | Last Updated:
 18 Nov 2026 - 09:46 am 
 FROM LEFT: Director of Events at Asian Cricket Council Usman Bajwa, Tournament Director Mohammed Al-Meer, Chief Executive Officer of Qatar Cricket Association Khalid Al-Suwaidi at a press conference yesterday.
 Follow
 us news
 Copy
 A+ 
 A- 
 The Peninsula 
 Doha, Qatar: The stage is set for the inaugural 50-over edition of the Asia Cup Rising Stars Cricket Tournament, with eight teams gearing up for 11 days of action-packed cricket in Doha from tomorrow.
 Qatar Cricket Association (QCA), under the supervision of the Asian Cricket Council (ACC), will host the tournament at West End International Cricket Stadium and the University of Doha for Science and Technology (UDST).
 The teams compete under two groups, with Group A featuring Pakistan Shaheens, India A, Nepal and the United Arab Emirates, while Sri Lanka A, Bangladesh A, Afghanistan A and Hong Kong, China, make up Group B.
 Speaking at the official media conference and trophy unveiling ceremony, QCA Board Member and Tournament Director Mohammed Abdullah Al Meer said Qatar was proud to host the competition for the second consecutive year.
 He highlighted the success of last year’s edition, which attracted more than 37,000 spectators, reached nearly 30 million viewers through live coverage and generated over 660 million social media engagements.
 “We are proud to host this tournament in Doha for the second year in a row. Last year was a great success, and we would like to thank the fans who came to the stadium and everyone who followed the tournament from home,” Al Meer said.
 He added that Qatar's experience in hosting major international sporting events, including the FIFA World Cup 2022, would help ensure a welcoming environment for teams, officials and spectators.
 “On behalf of the Qatar Cricket Association, I welcome all teams, players, officials and commercial partners to this edition of the DP World Asia Cup Rising Stars. We are proud to host this tournament for the second consecutive year,” he said.
 ACC representative Usman Bajwa thanked the QCA for its hospitality and support, highlighting the importance of the competition in providing a platform for emerging Asian cricketers.
 With eight teams in the line-up, Bajwa urged players to demonstrate sportsmanship and respect towards opponents, match officials and everyone involved in organising the tournament.
 “On behalf of the ACC, I would like to thank the Qatar Cricket Association for its efforts to stage a great tournament last year. The players are the main attraction of this tournament. I would urge the players to show respect to their opponents,” Bajwa said
 QCA Chief Executive Officer Khalid Al-Suwaidi said: “We are thrilled to have the Asian teams in Doha. We are here to announce the start of the DP World Asia Cup Rising Stars. We are pleased with the trust the ACC has placed in us. Welcome to all the players and officials. We saw some exciting cricket last year. I am sure it will be the same this year as well.”
 He also highlighted the significance of this year's edition, which will be the first 50-over tournament under the Asia Cup Rising Stars banner.
 "We look forward to an exciting competition and outstanding performances from all the participating teams," Al Suwaidi said.
 Last year’s edition was held in the T20 format, with Pakistan Shaheens defeating Bangladesh A in the final to claim the title.
